subject: Joint Hypothesis Testing Using the F-Statistic in SEM

messages.author: e5c4db1a1cffab6b
messages.subject: Joint Hypothesis Testing Using the F-Statistic in SEM
parts:
Dear all

Is there an easy way to do a joint hypothesis test and obtaining a bootstrap p-value in sem with laavan? In the example below, I would like to test the joint hypothesis that b1==b2==0 and obtain the bootstrapped p-value on the joint significance of ind60 and dem60 

  model <- ’ # measurement model 
 ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
 dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4 
dem65 =~ y5 + y6 + y7 + y8 
# regressions 
dem60 ~ ind60 
dem65 ~ b1 * ind60 + b2 * dem60 + control1 +control2 +control3
# residual correlations 
y1 ~~ y5 
y2 ~~ y4 + y6 
y3 ~~ y7 
y4 ~~ y8 
y6 ~~ y8
 ’  

Many thanks

parts:
I would prefer using a Wald test. I am aware that I can use  lavTestWald with the code below, but is it possible to obtain the bootstrapped p-value of the joint test?

fit<- sem(model,    data = model6.data,     estimator="dwls",   
                              se="bootstrap", bootstrap= 1000)
con = '
     b1 == 0
     b2  == 0
 '
lavTestWald(estimates_mobility_6, constraints = con)

messages.author: b8fd92e5e3662745
messages.subject: Re: Joint Hypothesis Testing Using the F-Statistic in SEM
parts:
The p-value is computed under the null. What you have is estimation under the alternative. Bootstrap is inherently an estimation method, not a testing method. (There's Bollen-Stine bootstrap... which is Beran-Srivastava bootstrap... under the null; but you have to make some strong assumptions that you can rotate your data as you please with it.) You can get bootstrap standard errors, but that's not the bootstrap p-value.
